dispatch_one routes an outbound mutation with a pre-existing binding to update_issue/add_comment/etc.; without a binding it generates a create mutation instead, which lands a NEW DC issue and passes the oracle for the wrong reason.
findings.finding: The plan specifies 14 outbound mutation cells (rows 2-13: edit summary, edit description, transition status, add/remove label, add comment, assign/unassign, create/delete link, set parent, clear parent) that are all UPDATE-type mutations — they require a pre-existing local ticket already bound to a DC issue. The scrub mechanism deliberately removes ALL bindings from the copied store. The plan does not specify any fixture or setup step that re-establishes a local↔DC binding before each outbound UPDATE cell runs. Without a binding, `outbound_differ.py:518-520` routes every ticket to the CREATE path (not UPDATE), so the edit, status, label, comment, assignee, link, and parent outbound cells would all either create a new issue or operate on a wrongly-created one — the edit oracle (`fields.summary` on the DC issue) would pass against the freshly-created issue, not the one the test intended to mutate. Rows 1 (create) and 14 (delete) are structurally fine. Rows 2-13 outbound are broken by design unless a binding-acquisition step is specified.
findings.location: DC-side mutation suite section; mutation oracle table rows 2-13 outbound direction
scenarios: Test author writes row 5 (add label outbound): edits a local ticket's tags, runs outbound pass. The reconciler sees no binding, emits outbound CREATE (not UPDATE), creates a new DC issue with the label already on it. The oracle reads `fields.labels` and finds the label — passes. But no edit was tested; a create was.
Test author writes row 8 (assign outbound): the reconciler creates a new issue with the assignee rather than updating the existing one. Oracle passes spuriously.
Row 14 (delete outbound): requires a binding to be present before the local delete triggers outbound delete — same structural gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a standard fixture `bound_dc_issue(dc_rebar_repo, transport, jira_dc_project)` that: (1) creates a DC issue via `transport.create_issue`; (2) runs a writing-mode inbound pass to mint the local ticket and binding; (3) returns `(local_id, dc_key)`. Each outbound UPDATE cell uses this fixture as its setup step, mutates `local_id` locally, runs the outbound pass, and reads `dc_key` on DC. Row 14 (outbound delete) also needs this fixture: establish binding, then delete the local ticket, then run outbound pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the pagination-seeding fixture's scope (recommend session-scoped), define whether seeded issues are deleted in teardown, and assert that the page-size probe runs exactly once before any seeding modifies the harness state.
evidence: 'Seed via `dc_transport.create_issue` in a pytest fixture (the same call the existing live cells use — not a raw REST POST, so the seeding path is one the adapter actually supports), collecting the returned keys into a `seeded_keys` set.'
'After the inbound pass, `recovered_count` is the number of `seeded_keys` for which a local ticket exists at `_jira_key_to_local_id(key)`; the assertion is `recovered_count == len(seeded_keys)`.'
No mention of fixture scope (session/module/function) anywhere in the plan.
No mention of a teardown or cleanup step that deletes seeded issues from the harness.
findings.finding: The pagination-seeding pytest fixture's scope is unspecified. The plan says 'Seed via `dc_transport.create_issue` in a pytest fixture … collecting the returned keys into a `seeded_keys` set' but never names the scope (session / module / function). If the fixture is function-scoped and multiple tests reference it, it re-executes for each test: a new batch of 2*observed+1 issues is created, the prior batch is never deleted (no retirement path), and the harness accumulates O(N_tests × page_size) issues within a single session. The `recovered_count == len(seeded_keys)` assertion is satisfied per-invocation (it only checks keys from the current batch), so the accumulation is SILENT — the test passes while the harness grows. The 'observe page size' probe is also re-executed each time, and its result may differ once the harness has hundreds of issues from prior fixture calls. This is a T9 lifecycle gap: no RETIRE path for seeded issues and no ownership/scope definition for the fixture.
findings.location: AC: 'the effective server page size is OBSERVED and reported … the suite seeds at least `2 * observed + 1` issues IN THE HARNESS' / 'Seed via `dc_transport.create_issue` in a pytest fixture … collecting the returned keys into a `seeded_keys` set'
scenarios: Function-scoped fixture called by 5 test functions: 5 × (2×50+1) = 505 issues created, 0 deleted; the page-size probe on the 5th call observes a harness with 500+ extra issues, potentially changing the observed cap and invalidating the '2*observed+1' threshold for that call, while all per-invocation assertions still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the seeding fixture `scope='session'` and add a `yield`/finaliser that deletes all keys in `seeded_keys` via `dc_transport.delete_issue` (or equivalent) after the session. Run the page-size probe as a module-level constant captured before any seeding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly prohibit parallel test execution for the mutation suite (e.g. mark all mutation tests with `@pytest.mark.serial` or document that the suite must be invoked with `-p no:xdist`), and state that the single fresh-git-repo binding store is owned exclusively by one sequential test process.
evidence: 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR ROW 14 — the probe is NOT emitted by a delete alone … A binding must therefore exist BEFORE the issue is deleted, so the cell must run: (1) create the issue in DC; (2) run a WRITING-MODE inbound pass … (3) delete the issue in DC; (4) run the `--mode dry-run` pass'
'the working repo in CI has NO git remote, asserted by a test' — the working repo is a single shared repo instance for the session
No mention of `pytest-xdist`, `--forked`, `pytest-ordering`, or any other mechanism that enforces sequential execution across mutation cells.
The binding store is a single `.tickets-tracker/` directory in the fresh git repo; concurrent writes to it from two reconciler subprocesses are not atomic.
findings.finding: The mutation suite's row-14 sequence (create → writing-mode inbound pass → delete → dry-run probe) and the shared fresh-git-repo binding store are both sensitive to test-execution order, yet the plan does not prohibit parallel test execution (e.g. `pytest-xdist`). If two mutation cells run concurrently against the same fresh git repo, they share the same binding store and `.tickets-tracker/` directory. Specifically: (a) a concurrent writing-mode inbound pass from another cell can write bindings for issues that row 14's delete step has not yet created, causing the dry-run probe to emit unexpected entries; (b) the row-14 sequence (step 2 is a writing-mode pass that must complete before step 3 deletes the issue) is broken if step 2 of another cell's pass interleaves with steps 1-3 of row 14. The plan requires sequential ordering via its 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR ROW 14' note but never enforces it by declaring a serialisation constraint on the test suite.
findings.location: Section 'The DC-side mutation suite' / AC row 14 'REQUIRED SEQUENCING FOR ROW 14' / Scope: 'tests/external/live_jira_dc/ — the mutation suite and its fixtures'
scenarios: Developer adds `pytest-xdist` (`-n auto`) to speed up the external suite: row 14's write-mode inbound pass (step 2) races with another cell's inbound pass; the binding store is written by both simultaneously; row 14's dry-run probe either misses the expected probe entry (the binding wasn't committed before step 3) or finds spurious entries from the concurrent cell, causing the jq assertion to fail or, worse, to pass with an incorrect binding.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` marker `serial` and a conftest guard that fails if `xdist` is active for this test module. Alternatively, give each mutation cell its own isolated fresh repo (separate `tmp_path`-backed git init) so that concurrent execution is safe by construction.

The Jira REST v2 issue-properties GET endpoint returns `{"key": "local_id", "value": <stored_value>}` per Jira Server documentation — but this shape has not been asserted against DC 8.17.1 in any existing live test; it is Partially-verified against general Jira knowledge

findings.finding: The Row 1 outbound oracle requires `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/local_id` against the DC 8.17.1 harness, but this specific endpoint surface has never been exercised live. The WRITE path (`set_entity_property` -> `client.add_issue_property`) is verified live (CI run 30662366152). The GET for a property value (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/{propertyKey}`) is a standard Jira Server REST v2 endpoint, but it is a distinct HTTP surface, separate OAuth scope handling is not required on DC (Basic auth is used), and the plan's direction to 'go direct' (via a raw REST call, not the transport) is correct — the transport has no getter. However, the endpoint's actual response shape on DC 8.17.1 (e.g., whether the body is `{"value": <scalar>}` or `<scalar>` directly) is unconfirmed. If the DC 8.17.1 harness wraps the value in a `{"value": …}` envelope (the standard Jira issue-properties response shape) the assertion must unwrap it, and if it does not, a wrapping assertion will fail silently. The plan does not state the expected response shape.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — oracle table row 1 outbound: 'entity property `local_id` read by RAW REST — `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/local_id`'
scenarios: If DC 8.17.1 wraps the property value in `{"value": …}` (standard Jira shape) and the test asserts `body == local_id` rather than `body["value"] == local_id`, the oracle always fails even when the outbound create is correct — a false red that looks like a product defect.
If the harness returns the value bare (no envelope) and the test unwraps it, the assertion always fails for the opposite reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line probe test or a note to the README: `status, body = _admin_request(f'/rest/api/2/issue/{key}/properties/local_id')` after a `set_entity_property` write; assert `body['value'] == expected_local_id` (standard Jira Server v2 shape). findings.finding: The plan asserts the `scanned=` line is 'emitted ONLY as a human-readable STDERR line by run_differs.py:282' and instructs the AC to 'capture STDERR (not stdout, which carries the JSON)' when parsing `invariants: scanned=(\d+)`. Both claims are factually wrong. (1) The `print(f"invariants: scanned=...")` call at run_differs.py:281-283 has NO `file=sys.stderr` argument — it goes to STDOUT. (2) In dry-run mode (`--mode dry-run`, which sets `persist=False`), `skip_invariant_filing = True` and the code takes the skipped branch, emitting only the `skipped` variant to stderr — the `scanned=` line is NEVER emitted. Since the plan ties the `scanned > 0` assertion to a dry-run pass (the same pass used to assert zero deletion/update counts), the assertion as written will never find the line in stderr and will always fail — silently passing only if the test simply ignores the missing line rather than asserting on it.
findings.location: AC: 'the store under test is a COPY of this project's real ticket store, and the pass reports `scanned` > 0' and the WHERE explanation beneath it
findings.suggested_fix: Split into two passes: (1) a writing-mode pass whose STDOUT is searched for `invariants: scanned=(\d+)` with N > 0; (2) a separate dry-run pass whose STDOUT JSON is parsed for zero delete/update counts. Alternatively, parse the dry-run stderr for `invariants: skipped (no-write mode, (\d+) issues in snapshot)` — that line IS on stderr and IS emitted in dry-run mode, and its captured integer proves the store is non-empty.

findings.finding: The `scanned > 0` AC incorrectly specifies both the stream and the format for asserting non-empty store coverage. The plan says 'capture STDERR (not stdout, which carries the JSON) and parse that line — e.g. match `invariants: scanned=(\d+)`', citing run_differs.py:282. But the actual code at run_differs.py:270-283 shows: (a) in dry-run mode (persist=False, the mode recommended for the zero-counts AC just below), the line printed is `'invariants: skipped (no-write mode, N issues in snapshot)'` on STDERR — the `scanned=` format is never emitted; (b) in writing mode (persist=True), the `scanned=` line IS printed (line 281-283) but WITHOUT `file=sys.stderr`, sending it to STDOUT. An implementer following the AC as written will assert on the wrong stream in writing mode, and will find the `scanned=` pattern is absent entirely in dry-run mode.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'scanned > 0' AC, sub-section 'WHERE scanned COMES FROM'
findings.suggested_fix: Use a writing-mode pass (e.g. `--mode bootstrap-strict`) for the `scanned > 0` assertion, and capture STDOUT (not STDERR). The regex `invariants: scanned=(\d+)` will appear on stdout after a writing-mode pass. Alternatively, in dry-run mode parse `invariants: skipped (no-write mode, (\d+) issues in snapshot)` from STDERR instead.

findings.finding: The `scanned > 0` AC specifies running `--mode dry-run` and parsing `invariants: scanned=(\d+)` from STDERR, but the code makes both claims simultaneously wrong. In dry-run mode `persist=False` (MODE_CAPS[DRY_RUN]=0, reconcile.py:222), so `skip_invariant_filing=True` (run_differs.py:270), and the only line emitted is `invariants: skipped (no-write mode, N issues in snapshot)` to STDERR (run_differs.py:275-278) — the `scanned=` form is never printed during dry-run. When `scanned=` IS emitted (writing modes only), it goes to STDOUT without `file=sys.stderr` (run_differs.py:281-283). An implementer following the plan's AC literally — regex `scanned=(\d+)` on STDERR of a dry-run pass — writes an assertion that will always fail (no match), not just on an empty store but on any store, silently certifying nothing.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'the store under test is a COPY … and the pass reports `scanned` > 0' bullet; also the WHERE `scanned` COMES FROM sub-note
findings.suggested_fix: Either: (1) change the AC to run a `bootstrap-strict` writing pass first, capture stdout, and match `invariants: scanned=(\d+)` on stdout (not stderr); or (2) assert store non-emptiness directly before the reconciler runs — e.g. count files under `.tickets-tracker/` or call `rebar list --repo-root <path>` and assert > 0 results — which is mode-independent and equally proves the copy was populated.
